3. Japan - Driver of the Day
URL: https://driveroftheday.com/race/japanese-grand-prix-2026
Mar 29, 2026 · Race results and driver ratings.

Oscar Piastri‘s performance in Sunday’s Japanese GP at the Suzuka International Racing Course saw him voted F1 Driver of the Day as he earned 18 big world championship points and the adulation of the fans.
Prior to the weekend, Piastri hadn’t completed a single racing lap, having failed to start in both Australia and China as McLaren struggled to adapt to the new regulations.
But it finally came good for the Melbourne-born talent, who put himself third on the grid behind the Mercedes duo of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell in Saturday’s qualifying before getting a great launch 24 hours later.
Piastri quickly put his foot down to take the lead into Turn 1 and proved comfortable once he got there, stretching out a lead of nearly two seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc and later Russell.
But any chance of Piastri keeping the lead went down the drain when the safety car came out on Lap 22 following Oliver Bearman’s shunt at Spoon Curve, handing the race to Antonelli on a silver platter.
Once the action got back underway on Lap 28, the Mercedes package, now in clear air, proved to be a cut above the Australian and his McLaren car as the 19-year-old quickly pulled away.
More from the Singapore GP
Catch up with Total Motorsport's latest Singapore GP coverage, including Max Verstappen's chaotic Sprint victory, the full Sprint Race classification, George Russell's potential grid penalty, and concerns over the physical demands of racing in Singapore.
While Piastri couldn’t live with Antonelli’s blistering pace on his way to his second consecutive Formula 1 victory, he was able to secure second as he landed the Driver of the Day honours at the 2026 Japanese GP.
“It would have been really interesting to see what would have happened without that [Safety Car],” Piastri said. “I could keep George behind and just before the stops we were actually pulling away a little bit again.
Antonelli reacts to taking lead of F1 world championship in Japan
Although Piastri will be relieved to finally get on the scoreboard, he will know McLaren have plenty of work to do to catch Mercedes and Antonelli in the remaining 20 rounds of the season.
After his dismal start, which dropped him out of the top three for the opening 10 laps, he slowly made his way through the order before profiting from the safety car to retake the lead that he held until the chequered flag.
Antonelli now leads the drivers’ championship for the first time in his career, becoming the youngest to ever do so, as he holds a nine point lead over Russell, who missed out on the podium places in Suzuka.
Heading into the month-long break on a high, he will look to continue extending his lead in May’s Miami GP in the United States whilst other teams will see the 33 days off as a chance to make some serious R&D inroads.
“It feels pretty good! Of course, it’s too early to think about the championship but we are on a good way,” Antonelli said, post-race. “I had a terrible start. I need to check what happened.
“Then I was lucky with the Safety Car to be in the lead but then the pace was incredible. It was really nice. The second stint I felt very good with the car. I’m very pleased with that.
“On the medium we were strong once we had free air and on the hard, the pace was incredible. I don’t know what the outcome would have been without the Safety Car but it made my life a lot easier.”

Oscar Piastri was voted Driver of the Day at the 2026 Japanese Grand Prix. 

FINAL: Oscar Piastri
